items.title: Best uniform polynomial error on a compact interval

references.title: Lloyd N. Trefethen, Approximation Theory and Approximation Practice, Chapter 10
references.locator: Printed pp. 73–74, best approximation problem and existence setup.

references.title: András Kroó and Allan Pinkus, Strong Uniqueness, §§4.2–4.4
references.locator: Printed pp. 18–22, finite-dimensional uniform approximation on a compact interval.

items.statement:
Let $I=[a,b]\subset\mathbb R$ with $a<b$, and let $C(I,\mathbb R)$ denote the
real-valued continuous functions on $I$. For $h\in C(I,\mathbb R)$ set
$\|h\|_{\infty,I}:=\sup_{x\in I}|h(x)|$. For $n\in\mathbb N_0$, let
$\mathcal P_n(I)$ be the restrictions to $I$ of real polynomials of degree at
most $n$, including the zero polynomial, and define
$$E_n(f;I):=\inf_{p\in\mathcal P_n(I)}\|f-p\|_{\infty,I}.$$
When $I=[-1,1]$, this agrees with the published definition
[[def-best-uniform-polynomial-approximation-error-and-chebyshev-interpolants]].

These quantities are finite and well-defined. The interval is compact by
[[thm-euclidean-heine-borel-pseudocompactness-and-extreme-values]], so each
continuous difference $f-p$ has a finite maximum absolute value. The
polynomial space contains $0$, hence the set of errors is nonempty and bounded
below by $0$; completeness of $\mathbb R$
([[def-complete-ordered-field]]) supplies its infimum.

items.title: A polynomial with the sign pattern of the active extrema

references.title: Lloyd N. Trefethen, Approximation Theory and Approximation Practice, Chapter 10
references.locator: Printed p. 74, the perturbation step in the proof of Theorem 10.1.

references.title: András Kroó and Allan Pinkus, Strong Uniqueness, §4.4

items.statement:
Let $I=[a,b]$ with $a<b$, let $e:I\to\mathbb R$ be continuous, and let
$E=\|e\|_{\infty,I}>0$. Put
$S_+=\{x\in I:e(x)=E\}$ and $S_-=\{x\in I:e(x)=-E\}$. If there are no
$n+2$ increasing points of $S_+\cup S_-$ with alternating signs, then there
is a real polynomial $h$ of degree at most $n$ such that
$e(x)h(x)>0$ for every $x\in S_+\cup S_-$.

items.title: Alternating polynomial signs force the Haar zero-count contradiction

references.title: Lloyd N. Trefethen, Approximation Theory and Approximation Practice, Chapter 10
references.locator: Printed pp. 73–75, Theorem 10.1 and its sign-change proof.

references.title: András Kroó and Allan Pinkus, Strong Uniqueness, §4.4
references.locator: Printed pp. 20–22, Theorem 4.4 for T-spaces; the polynomial specialization is proved locally here.

items.statement:
Let $n\ge0$, let $p$ be a nonzero real polynomial of degree at most $n$, and
let $x_0<\cdots<x_{n+1}$ be real numbers. The values $p(x_i)$ cannot all be
nonzero with alternating signs.

items.title: Polynomial coefficients are bounded by values at fixed distinct nodes

references.title: Tobin A. Driscoll and Richard J. Braun, Fundamentals of Numerical Computation, Polynomial interpolation
references.locator: Online chapter ‘Polynomial interpolation,’ Definition 2.1.1 and §2.1.1 (interpolation at distinct nodes as a Vandermonde system).

references.title: Lloyd N. Trefethen, Approximation Theory and Approximation Practice, Chapter 5
references.locator: Printed pp. 33–39, polynomial interpolation and cardinal formula.

items.statement:
Let $n\ge0$ and let $t_0,\ldots,t_n$ be distinct real numbers. For
$0\le j\le n$, define
$$L_j(x):=\prod_{k\ne j}\frac{x-t_k}{t_j-t_k}.$$
If $p(x)=\sum_{k=0}^{n}c_kx^k$ has degree at most $n$, then
$$p(x)=\sum_{j=0}^{n}p(t_j)L_j(x).$$
Consequently, writing $L_j(x)=\sum_{k=0}^{n}\ell_{jk}x^k$, every coefficient
satisfies
$$|c_k|\le\left(\sum_{j=0}^{n}|\ell_{jk}|\right)\max_{0\le j\le n}|p(t_j)|.$$
The empty product convention gives $L_0=1$ when $n=0$.

items.title: Alternating interpolation weights annihilate lower-degree polynomials

references.title: András Kroó and Allan Pinkus, Strong Uniqueness, §6.5
references.locator: Printed pp. 45–46, Lagrange interpolation weights used to prove uniqueness.

references.title: Lloyd N. Trefethen, Approximation Theory and Approximation Practice, Chapter 24
references.locator: Printed pp. 205–207, uniqueness argument for rational best approximants.

items.statement:
Let $N\ge0$ and let $x_0<\cdots<x_{N+1}$ be real nodes. Set
$\omega(t)=\prod_{j=0}^{N+1}(t-x_j)$ and
$w_i=\prod_{j\ne i}(x_i-x_j)$. If $g$ is a real polynomial of degree at most
$N$, then
$$\sum_{i=0}^{N+1}\frac{g(x_i)}{w_i}=0.$$
If, for one fixed $\varepsilon\in\{-1,1\}$, the values
$\varepsilon(-1)^i g(x_i)$ are all nonnegative, then $g$ is the zero
polynomial.

items.title: Reduced real rational representations are unique up to scale

references.title: András Kroó and Allan Pinkus, Strong Uniqueness, §6.2
references.locator: Printed pp. 43–44, reduced rational representations in Lemma 6.2.

references.title: Lloyd N. Trefethen, Approximation Theory and Approximation Practice, Chapter 24
references.locator: Printed pp. 199–200, rational functions in lowest terms and defect.

items.statement:
Call a pair $(p,q)$ of real polynomials reduced when $q\ne0$ and no
nonconstant polynomial divides both entries. We identify $p/q$ and $p'/q'$ as
the same rational function exactly when $pq'=p'q$. Every quotient with
nonzero denominator has a reduced representation, and any two reduced
representations of the same nonzero rational function differ by a common
nonzero real scalar. The zero rational function has reduced pair $(0,1)$ up to
a nonzero scalar. For $q(x)=\sum_{j=0}^{d}q_jx^j$, define
$\|q\|_{\mathrm{coef},2}:=(\sum_{j=0}^{d}q_j^2)^{1/2}$, unchanged by
appending zero coefficients. If $I$ is a nonempty interval, two reduced
representations of the same rational function with denominators strictly
positive on $I$ and coefficient norm $1$ are equal.

items.title: Weighted rational minimax families and defect

references.title: Lloyd N. Trefethen, Approximation Theory and Approximation Practice, Chapter 24
references.locator: Printed pp. 199–200, real rational functions, reduced degrees, and defect.

references.title: András Kroó and Allan Pinkus, Strong Uniqueness, §6
references.locator: Printed pp. 43–44, the irreducible type-(m,n) family and defect.

items.statement:
Let $I=[a,b]$ with $a<b$, let $m,n\in\mathbb N_0$, and let
$f,w\in C(I,\mathbb R)$ with $w(x)>0$ for every $x\in I$. A normalized
reduced pair is a pair of real polynomials $p,q$ such that $q>0$ on $I$,
$\deg p\le m$, $\deg q\le n$, $p$ and $q$ have no nonconstant common
divisor, and
$$\|q\|_{\mathrm{coef},2}:=\left(\sum_{j=0}^{n}q_j^2\right)^{1/2}=1\quad\text{when }q(x)=\sum_{j=0}^{n}q_jx^j.$$
The zero rational function is represented by $(p,q)=(0,1)$. By
[[lem-na-reduced-rational-representation-unique]], each rational function
admissible under these conditions has exactly one normalized reduced pair.
Define
$$\mathcal R_{m,n}^+(I):=\{p/q:(p,q)\text{ is a normalized reduced pair}\}$$
and
$$E_{m,n}(f,w;I):=\inf_{r\in\mathcal R_{m,n}^+(I)}\|w(f-r)\|_{\infty,I}.$$
The family is nonempty because it contains $r=0$. For each admissible $r=p/q$,
$q>0$ on $I$ makes $r$ continuous by
[[thm-algebra-of-continuous-functions]], so $w(f-r)$ is continuous and bounded
on compact $I$. The infimum is therefore finite, bounded below by zero, and
exists as a real number by completeness of $\mathbb R$.

For $r=p/q\ne0$ in reduced form, put
$$d_{m,n}(r):=\min\{m-\deg p,\ n-\deg q\},\qquad N_{m,n}(r):=m+n-d_{m,n}(r).$$
For $r=0$, define $d_{m,n}(0):=n$ and hence $N_{m,n}(0):=m$. The integer
$d_{m,n}(r)$ is the defect. A candidate is **normal** when $d_{m,n}(r)=0$
and **defective** when $d_{m,n}(r)>0$. The alternation count associated with
the candidate is $N_{m,n}(r)+2$; it equals $m+n+2$ only in the normal case.

items.title: The Remez alternation linear system has a unique solution

references.title: Ricardo Pachón and Lloyd N. Trefethen, Barycentric-Remez Algorithms for Best Polynomial Approximation in the Chebfun System, §2.1
references.locator: Printed pp. 5–6, equation (2.6) and the trial reference system.

references.title: Lloyd N. Trefethen, Approximation Theory and Approximation Practice, Chapter 10
references.locator: Printed pp. 73–79, polynomial minimax and alternation.

items.statement:
Let $n\ge0$, let $I=[a,b]$ with $a<b$, let $f:I\to\mathbb R$ be any function,
and let $x_0<\cdots<x_{n+1}$ be distinct nodes in $I$. There is a unique pair
$(p,\lambda)\in\mathcal P_n(I)\times\mathbb R$ satisfying
$$p(x_i)+(-1)^i\lambda=f(x_i),\qquad 0\le i\le n+1.$$

items.title: Best uniform polynomial approximants exist

references.title: Lloyd N. Trefethen, Approximation Theory and Approximation Practice, Chapter 10
references.locator: Printed pp. 73–74, existence of a best polynomial approximant.

references.title: András Kroó and Allan Pinkus, Strong Uniqueness, §4
references.locator: Printed pp. 18–22, finite-dimensional uniform approximation.

items.statement:
Let $I=[a,b]$ with $a<b$, let $n\ge0$, and let $f\in C(I,\mathbb R)$. There
is a polynomial $p_*\in\mathcal P_n(I)$ such that
$\|f-p_*\|_{\infty,I}=E_n(f;I)$.

items.title: Exact polynomial equioscillation certifies best approximation

references.title: Lloyd N. Trefethen, Approximation Theory and Approximation Practice, Chapter 10
references.locator: Printed pp. 73–75, Theorem 10.1, equioscillation sufficiency.

references.title: András Kroó and Allan Pinkus, Strong Uniqueness, §4.4
references.locator: Printed pp. 20–22, Theorem 4.4, sufficiency for T-spaces.

items.statement:
Let $n\ge0$, let $f\in C([a,b],\mathbb R)$ with $a<b$, and let
$p\in\mathcal P_n([a,b])$. If $E:=\|f-p\|_{\infty,[a,b]}>0$ and there are
$n+2$ ordered nodes $x_0<\cdots<x_{n+1}$ in $[a,b]$ and a sign
$\sigma\in\{-1,1\}$ such
that
$$f(x_i)-p(x_i)=\sigma(-1)^iE\qquad(0\le i\le n+1),$$
then no polynomial in $\mathcal P_n([a,b])$ has smaller uniform error than
$p$. Thus the displayed residual values are an a posteriori optimality
certificate.

items.title: Finite-budget polynomial Remez exchange with an exact extrema oracle

references.title: Ricardo Pachón and Lloyd N. Trefethen, Barycentric-Remez Algorithms for Best Polynomial Approximation in the Chebfun System, §§2.1–2.2
references.locator: Printed pp. 5–7, trial alternation system and first/second Remez exchange.

references.title: Lloyd N. Trefethen, Approximation Theory and Approximation Practice, Chapter 10
references.locator: Printed pp. 73–79, best polynomial approximation and equioscillation.

items.statement:
**Inputs.** A nondegenerate interval $I=[a,b]$, a degree $n\ge0$, a continuous
real function $f$ on $I$, an integer exchange budget $B\in\mathbb N_0$, and an initial reference
$X=(x_0,\ldots,x_{n+1})$ with $a\le x_0<\cdots<x_{n+1}\le b$. Also supply an
exact extrema oracle for a polynomial candidate $p$. On each call it returns
one of:

- alternation$(E,y_0,\ldots,y_{n+1})$, only when $E=\|f-p\|_{\infty,I}$ and the
  returned ordered distinct nodes lie in $I$ and satisfy
  $f(y_i)-p(y_i)=\sigma(-1)^iE$ for one fixed sign $\sigma$;
- maximum$(E,y)$, only when $y\in I$, $E=\|f-p\|_{\infty,I}$ and
  $|f(y)-p(y)|=E$; or
- inconclusive, when neither exact certificate can be returned.

**Procedure.** For $k=0,\ldots,B$, solve the unique real linear system
$$p_k(x_i)+(-1)^i\lambda_k=f(x_i),\qquad 0\le i\le n+1,$$
for $p_k\in\mathcal P_n(I)$ and $\lambda_k\in\mathbb R$, using
[[lem-na-polynomial-remez-system-invertible]]. Query the oracle for $p_k$.
If it returns alternation$(0,Y)$ or maximum$(0,y)$, return exact$(p_k)$,
since either response certifies zero uniform error. If it returns
alternation$(E,Y)$ with $E>0$, return certified$(p_k,E,Y)$; the optimality
claim is discharged by [[thm-na-polynomial-equioscillation-certificate]]. If
it returns inconclusive, return oracle-inconclusive. If it returns
maximum$(E,y)$ with $E>0$ and $E=|\lambda_k|$, return certified$(p_k,E,X)$,
because the solved equations make $X$ an alternating set and the oracle
certifies the global norm. If $\lambda_k=0<E$, return zero-level-no-exchange.

In the remaining case, let $s=\operatorname{sgn}(f(y)-p_k(y))$. Find the
smallest index $i$ for which $s=\operatorname{sgn}(\lambda_k)(-1)^i$ and
replacing $x_i$ by $y$ preserves a strictly increasing reference tuple under
these tests: for $i=0$, require $a\leq y<x_1$; for $i=n+1$, require
$x_n<y\leq b$; and for $0<i<n+1$, require $x_{i-1}<y<x_{i+1}$. Thus a
global maximum at an endpoint may replace the corresponding endpoint reference
node, while distinctness and strict ordering are retained. Replace $x_i$ by
$y$ and continue. If no such index exists, return
no-order-preserving-exchange. If all $B+1$ iterations finish without a
certificate, return budget-exhausted with the last candidate and reference.

**Outputs.** The procedure returns an exact best-approximation certificate,
an exact zero-error candidate, or one of the explicit inconclusive,
zero-level, no-exchange, or budget statuses. It asserts no convergence of the
iterates. Any implementation must ensure each exact solve and oracle call
terminates.

items.title: The rational first-variation space has dimension set by defect

references.title: András Kroó and Allan Pinkus, Strong Uniqueness, Lemma 6.2
references.locator: Printed p. 44, dimension and T-space property of P_m+rP_n.

references.title: Lloyd N. Trefethen, Approximation Theory and Approximation Practice, Chapter 24
references.locator: Printed pp. 199–201, rational defect and numerator degree count.

items.statement:
Let $r=p/q\in\mathcal R_{m,n}^+(I)$ be nonzero, with its reduced pair and
defect $d=d_{m,n}(r)$, and put $N=m+n-d$. Then
$$\{u q-p v:u\in\mathcal P_m,\ v\in\mathcal P_n\}=\mathcal P_N.$$
For $r=0$ with the convention $p=0,q=1,d=n,N=m$, the same equality holds.

items.title: Best weighted rational approximants exist

references.title: Lloyd N. Trefethen, Approximation Theory and Approximation Practice, Chapter 24
references.locator: Printed pp. 205–206, rational best-approximation existence argument.

references.title: András Kroó and Allan Pinkus, Strong Uniqueness, §6.1
references.locator: Printed pp. 43–44, Theorem 6.1 and denominator-zero cancellation.

items.statement:
For $I=[a,b]$ with $a<b$, $m,n\ge0$, $f\in C(I,\mathbb R)$, and a strictly
positive continuous weight $w$, there is $r_*\in\mathcal R_{m,n}^+(I)$ such
that
$$\|w(f-r_*)\|_{\infty,I}=E_{m,n}(f,w;I).$$

items.title: A nonzero best polynomial error must alternate at n+2 extrema

references.title: Lloyd N. Trefethen, Approximation Theory and Approximation Practice, Chapter 10
references.locator: Printed pp. 74–75, necessity direction in Theorem 10.1.

references.title: András Kroó and Allan Pinkus, Strong Uniqueness, §4.4
references.locator: Printed pp. 20–22, necessity direction in Theorem 4.4.

items.statement:
Let $I=[a,b]$ with $a<b$, let $n\ge0$, and let $f\in C(I,\mathbb R)$. If
$p\in\mathcal P_n(I)$ is a best approximant with
$E:=\|f-p\|_{\infty,I}>0$, then there are $n+2$ ordered points
$x_0<\cdots<x_{n+1}$ in $I$ and $\sigma\in\{-1,1\}$ such that
$$f(x_i)-p(x_i)=\sigma(-1)^iE\qquad(0\le i\le n+1).$$

items.title: The best uniform polynomial approximant is unique

references.title: Lloyd N. Trefethen, Approximation Theory and Approximation Practice, Chapter 10
references.locator: Printed pp. 74–75, uniqueness proof following Theorem 10.1.

references.title: András Kroó and Allan Pinkus, Strong Uniqueness, §4.4
references.locator: Printed pp. 20–22, uniqueness consequences of alternation in a T-space.

items.statement:
For every $f\in C([a,b],\mathbb R)$ with $a<b$ and every $n\ge0$, there is
exactly one $p_*\in\mathcal P_n([a,b])$ with
$\|f-p_*\|_{\infty,[a,b]}=E_n(f;[a,b])$.

items.title: A budgeted polynomial Remez exchange terminates within its finite cap

references.title: Ricardo Pachón and Lloyd N. Trefethen, Barycentric-Remez Algorithms for Best Polynomial Approximation in the Chebfun System, §2
references.locator: Printed pp. 5–7, finite reference-set updates and trial solves.

references.title: Lloyd N. Trefethen, Approximation Theory and Approximation Practice, Chapter 10
references.locator: Printed pp. 73–79, polynomial Remez context.

items.statement:
For any finite integer budget $B\in\mathbb N_0$, the procedure
[[alg-na-minimax-approximation-and-remez-algorithms]] makes at most $B+1$
linear solves and at most $B+1$ oracle calls (at most $2(B+1)$ calls total) and
returns a status, provided each exact linear solve and each oracle call
terminates. This is a finite-budget termination statement, not an iterative
convergence theorem.

items.title: Weighted rational minimizers satisfy the defect-sensitive alternation criterion

references.title: Lloyd N. Trefethen, Approximation Theory and Approximation Practice, Chapter 24
references.locator: Printed pp. 199–207, defect-sensitive real rational equioscillation theorem and proof.

references.title: András Kroó and Allan Pinkus, Strong Uniqueness, §§6.2–6.5
references.locator: Printed pp. 44–46, rational perturbation dimension, alternation theorem, and uniqueness.

items.statement:
Let $I=[a,b]$ with $a<b$, let $m,n\ge0$, and let $f,w\in C(I,\mathbb R)$
with $w>0$ on $I$. A best rational approximant in
$\mathcal R_{m,n}^+(I)$ exists and is unique. For a candidate $r=p/q$ with
positive weighted error $E_r:=\|w(f-r)\|_{\infty,I}>0$, let
$N=N_{m,n}(r)=m+n-d_{m,n}(r)$. Then $r$ is best if and only if there are
$N+2$ ordered nodes $x_0<\cdots<x_{N+1}$ in $I$ and
$\sigma\in\{-1,1\}$ such that
$$w(x_i)(f(x_i)-r(x_i))=\sigma(-1)^iE_r\qquad(0\le i\le N+1).$$
If the best error is $0$, positivity of $w$ forces the unique best function
to be $f$ itself. In the normal case $d=0$ the count is $m+n+2$; for
defective candidates the count is $m+n+2-d$.

items.title: Finite-budget weighted rational Remez exchange with defect status

references.title: Silviu-Ioan Filip, Yuji Nakatsukasa, Lloyd N. Trefethen, and Bernhard Beckermann, Rational Minimax Approximation via Adaptive Barycentric Representations, §§3–4.1
references.locator: pp. A2432–A2436, rational Remez equations, normalization, and solve branches.

references.title: Lloyd N. Trefethen, Approximation Theory and Approximation Practice, Chapter 24
references.locator: Printed pp. 199–207, rational defect and alternation.

items.statement:
**Inputs.** A nondegenerate interval $I=[a,b]$, degrees $m,n\ge0$, continuous
real target $f$, strictly positive continuous weight $w$, a finite exchange
integer budget $B\in\mathbb N_0$, an initial reference
$X=(x_0,\ldots,x_{m+n+1})$ satisfying
$a\leq x_0<\cdots<x_{m+n+1}\leq b$, an
exact rational alternation-solver procedure, and an exact weighted-extrema
oracle.

The alternation solver is an explicit input procedure. On a reference
$X=(x_0,\ldots,x_{m+n+1})$, it solves the nonlinear equations
$$w(x_i)\bigl(f(x_i)-p(x_i)/q(x_i)\bigr)=(-1)^i\lambda$$
with $p,q$ coprime, $\deg p\le m$, $\deg q\le n$, $q>0$ on $I$, and
$\|q\|_{\mathrm{coef},2}=1$. It reports one of: a unique candidate with
defect $d=0$ and its solved level $\lambda$; an exact defective candidate
with its computed $d>0$ and solved level $\lambda$; singular or nonunique
system; no normal solution; or inconclusive. The procedure does not assume
that this nonlinear solve always succeeds.

The weighted-extrema oracle for a returned candidate $r=p/q$ reports one of:

- alternation$(E,Y)$ only when $E=\|w(f-r)\|_{\infty,I}$ and $Y$ consists of
  $N_{m,n}(r)+2$ ordered distinct points in $I$ with weighted residuals
  $\sigma(-1)^iE$;
- maximum$(E,x)$ only when $x\in I$, $E=\|w(f-r)\|_{\infty,I}$ and
  $|w(x)(f(x)-r(x))|=E$; or
- inconclusive.

**Procedure.** For $k=0,\ldots,B$, call the alternation solver on the current
reference. Return its singular, no-normal-solution, or inconclusive status
unchanged. If it returns a defective candidate, return
defective$(d,N_{m,n}(r))$ immediately; do not apply the normal
$m+n+2$-point count. For a normal candidate $(r,\lambda)$, query the
weighted-extrema oracle. If it returns inconclusive, return
oracle-inconclusive. A response alternation$(0,Y)$ or maximum$(0,x)$
returns exact$(r)$, since either certifies zero weighted error. An
alternation response with $E>0$ returns certified$(r,E,Y)$, with optimality supplied by
[[thm-na-weighted-rational-alternation-characterization]]. For maximum$(E,x)$
with $E=|\lambda|$, the current reference itself is an exact global
alternation certificate, so return certified$(r,E,X)$. If $\lambda=0<E$,
return zero-level-no-exchange. If $E>|\lambda|$,
exchange the returned maximum point $x$ for the smallest reference node $x_i$
whose expected sign $\operatorname{sgn}(\lambda)(-1)^i$ matches the sign of
$w(x)(f(x)-r(x))$ and for which replacing $x_i$ by $x$ preserves strict
ordering. If no such index exists, return no-valid-exchange. After $B+1$
unsuccessful iterations, return budget-exhausted.

**Outputs.** The procedure returns an exact minimax certificate, an exact
zero-error candidate, or an explicit defect, singularity, no-solution,
oracle, exchange, or budget status. It claims no existence of a successful
nonlinear solve and no iterative convergence.

items.title: A budgeted weighted rational Remez exchange terminates within its finite cap

references.title: Silviu-Ioan Filip, Yuji Nakatsukasa, Lloyd N. Trefethen, and Bernhard Beckermann, Rational Minimax Approximation via Adaptive Barycentric Representations, §§3–4
references.locator: pp. A2432–A2436, finite rational Remez solve and update branches.

items.statement:
For a finite integer budget $B\in\mathbb N_0$, the procedure
[[alg-na-weighted-rational-remez-exchange]] makes at most $B+1$ alternation
solver calls and at most $B+1$ extrema-oracle calls (at most $2(B+1)$ calls
total) and returns an explicit status, provided each input procedure
terminates. This does not assert that the nonlinear solver succeeds or that
the exchange iterates converge.

title: Minimax approximation and remez algorithms — Examples

items.title: A two-node degree-zero Remez certificate

references.title: Ricardo Pachón and Lloyd N. Trefethen, Barycentric-Remez Algorithms for Best Polynomial Approximation in the Chebfun System, §2
references.locator: Printed pp. 5–7, the trial reference equations and extremum exchange.

items.statement:
For $f(x)=|x|$ on $[-1,1]$, degree $n=0$, and initial nodes $x_0=0,x_1=1$,
the Remez linear system returns $p(x)=1/2$ and signed level $\lambda=-1/2$.
An exact global-extrema oracle returns error $1/2$, so the current reference is
an optimality certificate.

items.title: The degree-one minimax approximation to x squared

references.title: Lloyd N. Trefethen, Approximation Theory and Approximation Practice, Chapter 10
references.locator: Printed pp. 73–79, best polynomial approximation and equioscillation.

items.statement:
On $[-1,1]$, the unique best degree-one uniform approximation to $f(x)=x^2$
is the constant polynomial $p(x)=1/2$, with error $1/2$.

items.title: A defective rational minimizer can have fewer than m+n+2 extrema

references.title: Lloyd N. Trefethen, Approximation Theory and Approximation Practice, Chapter 24
references.locator: Printed pp. 199–207, defect-sensitive rational alternation.

references.title: András Kroó and Allan Pinkus, Strong Uniqueness, §6
references.locator: Printed pp. 43–46, defective type-(m,n) rational approximants.

items.statement:
Every best real rational approximant of type $(m,n)$ with positive error has
at least $m+n+2$ distinct alternating global extrema.
